newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSE BOOK ON RUSSIAN BOND COMPENSATION.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSE BOOK ON RUSSIAN BOND COMPENSATION.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Thursday it had given up hope of pursuading Moscow to compensate Dutch holders of pre-revolution Russian bonds.

Finance Ministry spokesman Raymond Salet said the Dutch authorities had tried unsuccessfully to win payment on behalf of Dutch investors in the bonds with a nominal value of about 950 million guilders. "We will not take any action. It's a closed chapter," he told Reuters.
France last year won compensation of about $400 million over four years for its holders of Tsarist bonds issued before the Bolshevik revolution of 1917.
Dutch small investors lobby group VEB said earlier this month it had asked the Dutch foreign affairs and finance ministers to take action to clinch a similar deal for the Dutch.
"We tried it before but we have no chance of success," said Salet.
